stem: In the lesson “Joints and Coordinate Systems”, which description correctly defines “Joint position”?
option_a: The rate at which a joint position changes
option_b: The position value of each individual joint
option_c: Describing the robot state using joint variables
option_d: The familiar angle unit that must be converted correctly when talking to an API
explanation: Joint position is the value of each joint, usually an angle for this arm. It describes the state joint by joint, which is different from the rate of change (velocity) or from where the gripper is in space.

stem: Choose the most accurate description of “Joint velocity” in the context of Joints and Coordinate Systems.
option_a: The last element of the kinematic chain, which acts on the environment
option_c: The rate at which a joint position changes
option_d: The standard pose defined as the starting point of an exercise

option_c: The familiar angle unit that must be converted correctly when talking to an API

stem: In the lesson “Joints and Coordinate Systems”, which description correctly defines “Cartesian space”?
option_a: The angle unit commonly used in simulation libraries
option_c: The standard pose defined as the starting point of an exercise
option_d: The position value of each individual joint
explanation: Cartesian space describes position along coordinate axes such as x, y and z, typically for the end effector. It is the "where in the world" view; joint space is the "how each joint is set" view.
